requirement:
In authored book chapters, a passage opted into citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary` displays its
body as ordinary Markdown prose, with the same left alignment as the
surrounding prose and no opening citation badge or enclosing border.

A small marker in the right gutter identifies the passage's citation-checking
annotations. It does not claim that recorded evidence is current or accepted.
The outermost eligible citation fence has one marker; nested commentary
belongs to its list rather than displaying another marker.

Activating the marker opens the list of resolved citations from the source
passage, including its opening citation, citation-only metadata paragraphs,
and citations within nested commentary. Citations belonging to nested
requirement or example declarations are excluded. Repeated citations appear
once. Project citations link to their declarations; built-in citations retain
their descriptive hover text. The marker is keyboard operable, has an
accessible label, and shows visible keyboard focus. Opening the list does not
hide the passage. Inline citations within explanatory prose retain their
usual rendering.

Rendering does not change the source passage, its discovered references, or
its review inputs. Unfenced citations, citations inside requirement or example
declarations, and utility-only commentary retain their existing rendering.
rationale:
I judge the two marked tests adequate for `requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display`. The two tests are `reviewed_passages_show_one_gutter_list_and_preserve_prose_and_literal_contexts` and `citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details`, both in `src/lib.rs` under `mod[tests]`. I did not request implementation source. The expected results below come from the requirement text. **Body shown as ordinary prose, with no opening badge or border** - In `reviewed_passages_show_one_gutter_list_and_preserve_prose_and_literal_contexts`, pulldown_cmark renders `

Nested prose.

` and `

The ordinary paragraph cites…`. The raw `::::{cite}` fence text is absent from the prose. - In `citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details`, the `:::{cite} rules.ready` case checks that `alt="cite rules.ready"` appears exactly once in the whole chapter. That one occurrence is in the annotation block before ``, so the prose has no opening badge. The same test checks that `rules.other` and `habeas:util` are absent from the visible prose. - The CSS assertions require `border: 0;` and `padding: 0;` on `.habeas-citation-passage`. They parse the margin shorthand and require a left margin of `0`, which covers the "same left alignment" clause. **Marker in the right gutter, one per outermost fence** - Exactly one `habeas-citation-passage` and one `habeas-citation-list` are expected, even though the source has nested `::::{cite}` fences, nested declarations, and other fences. - CSS assertions cover `position: relative` on the passage, `position: absolute` and `right:` (with no `left:`) on the marker, and the `max-width` and `position: absolute` panel. **List contents** - The list has exactly 4 `

  • ` entries: `habeas:util`, `rules.other`, `rules.ready`, and `rules.term_rule`. This covers the opening citation (`habeas:util`), the citation-only metadata paragraph (`rules.other`), and citations in nested commentary (the nested `{cite}` fence and the definition container, which gives `rules.term_rule`). - `rules.inside` is absent from the list. It is cited only in the nested req and example declarations, an inline code span, an escaped citation, and a fenced code block, and each of those is excluded. - `rules.ready` is cited several times but listed once, which covers deduplication. - Project citations link to `rules.html#habeas-req-rules.other`, and the built-in citation keeps its `habeas-builtin" title=` hover text. **Accessibility and keyboard** - The `` carries `aria-label="Show citations for this passage"`. - A CSS assertion checks `summary:focus-visible` for `outline: 2px solid var(--links);`. - The marker is a native `
    `/`` element. I count this as keyboard operable, since the tests check no JavaScript and the requirement does not call for any. **Opening the list does not hide the passage** - The test asserts `
    \n

    The ordinary paragraph…`, so the prose follows the disclosure as a sibling. **Inline citations and other contexts keep their rendering** - The outside paragraph's `rules.inside` citation stays an inline badge, with a link and an `alt` attribute, and it stays outside the passage and the list. - The inline `rules.ready` citation inside the passage stays once in the prose. - The nested req and example keep their `aria-label` and `href`, and their detail chapters keep their citation badges. - The utility-only fence keeps its `habeas-fenced-ref` rendering with the built-in badge. - The unresolved citation, the HTML-literal fence, the unclosed fence, and the code fence all remain verbatim. - `citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details` covers other container kinds (req, example, definition, note, cite, impl, test) and checks that the detail chapters keep their badges. **Source unchanged** - Both tests check that the file on disk and `text_references` are unchanged after preprocessing. The first test also checks that declaration texts are unchanged. I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that contradicts the requirement. The one clause I did not trace to a test is that the marker "does not claim that recorded evidence is current or accepted". That is a negative statement about the marker's meaning, with no checkable behavior beyond the marker content the tests already examine.

::::{req} citation_review.book_commentary
A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.
The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.
The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
